method.description: Role and mapping resolution for the Colorado conduct-no-longer-prohibited form set (C.R.S. § 24-72-711). The two assigned reconciliation questions were answered from the form-face evidence already recorded in this repository — official titles, form-face revision strings, roles, byte identities and technical structure carried by the source-artifact registry, the repository asset audit, the nationwide source inventory and the adopted Edition 1.2 asset rows — corroborated against the Colorado Judicial Branch's own published form index. No binary was downloaded, extracted, materialized, copied or reconstructed; no receipt was written; Edition 1.2 was not mutated; no component was rebound; no legal conclusion was drawn.
method.binaryDeposition: No binary was retrieved or deposited. This job's ownedPaths are limited to this single production-factory JSON file.
method.byteVerificationNote: Both documents read presence=missing in the working tree at their pre-batch-1 inventory paths and are held only under private/, which is untracked. The SHA-256 and byte values reproduced below are the digests the adopted Edition 1.2 asset rows and the source-artifact registry already carry, and they agree with each other exactly. They are reproduced as identity of record, not as a fresh byte measurement of an issuer-served file.

assignedQuestions.answer: JDF 2370 is the issuer's guide — instructions. It cannot satisfy a primary_filing component. The existing binding is a role mismatch and is confirmed as such.

assignedQuestions.question: Which retained Colorado document carries the primary_filing (motion) role for the conduct-no-longer-prohibited track, and is it the presently unbound JDF 2371?

evidence: Adopted Edition 1.2 retains three distinct assets for this statutory family and assigns each a distinct role: CO:JDF-2370:INSTRUCTIONS:EN (assetClass instructions), CO:JDF-2371:MOTION:EN (assetClass packet_form) and CO:JDF-2374:ORDER:EN (assetClass packet_form). The roles are carried by the edition rows themselves, not inferred from filenames.

The recorded form-face evidence separates the two documents on title and on structure. JDF 2370's face title is 'Guide to Sealing Conviction Records - Conduct No Longer Prohibited' and it carries 6 logical AcroForm fields across 2 pages — a guide with a handful of caption fields. JDF 2371's face title is 'Motion to Seal Conviction Records - Conduct No Longer Prohibited' and it carries 51 logical AcroForm fields — a completable filing. A 6-field guide cannot receive the participant data a 51-field motion collects.
Both documents carry the identical form-face revision string 'R: July 1, 2025', so the pair is co-revised and the role difference is not a revision artefact.

The source-artifact registry independently classifies the two by role: JDF 2370 role='official guide', sourceTreatment='reference_only', packageTier='reference-only', runtimeEligibility='ineligible_never_a_participant_filing_artifact'; JDF 2371 role='participant court form', sourceTreatment='form_candidate', packageTier='forms'.

JDF 2371 is bound to no component anywhere in data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-source-relationships.json. The only two CO relationships for this track bind primary-filing-1 to JDF-2370 and proposed-order-2 to JDF-2374, so the motion is orphaned while the guide is over-bound.

The adopted CO legal-design memo already records, as a note on the primary_filing component, 'The conduct-no-longer-prohibited set is JDF 2370, 2371 and 2374.' The memo names the set; the edition resolves which member carries which role. This job reads the memo as corroboration and does not alter it.

The issuer's own published form index corroborates the split: the Colorado Judicial Branch publishes JDF 2370 as the Guide, JDF 2371 as the Motion and JDF 2374 as the Order at https://www.coloradojudicial.gov/sites/default/files/2025-07/, and its July 2025 forms blotter records all three as new forms released 1 July 2025 in response to HB24-1133.

scopeFinding.question: Is JDF 2371 a statewide Colorado form or a county-local form?
scopeFinding.why: JDF is the Colorado Judicial Department form series. The forms are drafted and published centrally by the Colorado Judicial Branch for use in every judicial district and are served from a single statewide index, not from any district or county court site. The statute they implement, C.R.S. § 24-72-711, applies statewide, and the adopted CO legal-design memo records geography.scope=statewide for this track.

contradictedRegistryFlag.explanation: The court_specific classification is driven entirely by the single marker service_city_state_zip — a certificate-of-service address block containing city, state and ZIP fields. Every Colorado motion that must be served on the district attorney carries that block, including statewide JDF forms. The marker evidences a service block, not a county-specific form. The sibling guide JDF 2370, which has no service block, was scored statewide by the same scanner, which is the tell.

contradictedRegistryFlag.correctionRequired: Set geographicScope=statewide and currency to a non-local value for this artifact row. Recorded as a handoff, not applied.

scopeFinding.doNotInfer: This finding resolves the scope of JDF 2371 only. It does not resolve where a participant files, which remains the court holding the conviction records, and it does not convert any local-scope finding elsewhere in the Colorado backlog.

edition13Impact.whyNoAmendment: The adopted Edition 1.2 rows for both documents are already correct. CO:JDF-2370:INSTRUCTIONS:EN is correctly typed as instructions and CO:JDF-2371:MOTION:EN is correctly typed as a packet_form motion, both at the correct revision and at bytes this job confirms against two independent recorded measurements. The defect was never in the edition; it was in the repository-side component-to-document mapping and in a heuristic scope flag on a registry row. Neither is edition content. This job therefore contributes a satisfied dependency to the Edition 1.3 publication gate and adds nothing to the amendment handoff.
